lessons.title: Customer Service and Contact Center
lessons.why: Dynamics 365 Contact Center is Microsoft’s CCaaS. Customer Service is not automatically that product.
depends: a reason to have a queue of strangers
body: Dynamics 365 Contact Center can stand alone or embed with Customer Service. Voice in that product uses Azure Communication Services. An auto attendant in Teams is not this product. A trial click-path is not a design: emergency calling, recording, and a busy hour are still gates.
AB-250 is the exam that matches this work. MB-280 was a Sales and Customer Insights exam and it retired on 31 July 2026. Do not revise the wrong guide.
lessons.say: Contact Center is the CCaaS. A Teams auto attendant is not. AB-250 is the exam. MB-280 is retired and was the wrong scope anyway.
lessons.fault: A pilot turns on Copilot and never defines a queue.
lessons.listen: Dynamics 365 Contact Center is the contact-center product. Do not call a Teams auto attendant by that name.

lessons.title: Channels
lessons.why: AB-250 weights channel implementation at about 30 to 35 percent, the largest published slice.
body: Voice, chat, and the other channels are the job. The study guide’s channel section is larger than the agent-and-AI section. Spend the hours there. Voice still needs numbers, a workstream, and a human path.

Proactive outbound and real-time translation exist as channel behaviors. Outbound needs consent and a caller ID you mean to present. Translation does not replace a human language queue when policy requires one.

lessons.title: Unified routing
lessons.why: Work items do not magically find experts. Classification and capacity do that, or fail to.
body: A workstream takes the item in. Classification sets language, intent, or priority. Queues hold the items. Assignment uses skills, capacity, and presence-like availability. A French billing item should not land in a general English queue because you forgot the rule.
Skills must exist on the representatives, not only on a slide. If every item requires a skill nobody has, the queue never assigns. Unknown intent needs a default human queue, not a retry loop.
lessons.say: Workstream, classification, queue, assignment. Unknown intent has a human default.
lessons.fault: French callers reach the English queue, or every item waits for a skill nobody has.
lessons.listen: Unified routing classifies a work item, then assigns it to someone with capacity. Give unknown a human queue.

lessons.title: Representative experience and Copilot
lessons.why: The person answering needs a console, a role, and assistance that quotes sources you trust.
body: AB-250 calls this the representative experience: presence in the product, the session, productivity tools, and Copilot assists such as summaries. A user who can open the app and belongs to no queue is not a representative yet.
Copilot that summarizes the wrong case, or quotes a stale article, is worse than silence. Connect knowledge sources you stand behind. The assist is not the PSTN route and not the emergency path.
lessons.say: Copilot assists the representative. It is not the route, and its sources have to be true.
lessons.fault: The agent sends a Copilot reply from a retired price list.
lessons.listen: Give representatives a role, a queue, and Copilot sources you are willing to defend.

lessons.title: Voice on ACS
lessons.why: The contact-center voice channel is not a Teams call queue with a different logo.
body: Dynamics 365 Contact Center voice is built with Azure Communication Services. Teams Phone extensibility lets some of those designs reuse the customer’s Teams Phone investment so the agent is not on a second phone system. The Tech Community post names that direction. Confirm the current setup guide before you promise it.
Transfers to a Teams expert still need that expert to be a real Teams Phone user with a number, in the Connect model’s own wording. Do not assume the contact-center license covered them.

chart.title: Two phone systems or one
chart.note: Extensibility is how you avoid two.

lessons.say: Contact Center voice runs on ACS. Teams Phone extensibility is how you avoid a second phone, when the design is actually certified for it.
lessons.fault: Two phones ring the same agent.
lessons.listen: Contact-center voice uses ACS. Use Teams Phone extensibility only when that design is the one you bought.

lessons.title: The AB-250 map
lessons.why: The published weights tell you where to spend the week.
body: As of the study guide accessed 14 October 2026, the skills are deploy 15–20, channels 30–35, agents and AI 10–15, work distribution 10–15, representative experience 15–20, and analytics 10–15. Passing score is 700. The public page allows 120 minutes.
The beta discount ran through 18 June 2026. Treat the exam as the live contact-center certification and confirm the seat on Learn the week you book. Practice tests for MB-280 will not prepare you.
